title: decision: sequence the personal MIMI drafts, do not merge them
description:
Mark asked (2026-11-26) whether to merge or consolidate his personal
MIMI I-Ds. Recorded so the question is not reopened.

## What exists

- ~/PROJECT/ietf-mimi-provider-auth, draft-atwood-mimi-provider-auth
  (780 md lines): DNS-key RFC 9421 signatures, DANE, PKIX mTLS, trust
  lists, DID manifests. protocol-07 §4 material.
- ~/PROJECT/ietf-mimi-catchup, draft-atwood-mimi-catchup (16 pages,
  written 2026-11-26): the fanout sequence, catchUp, and the
  requirement that unrecoverable loss be reported. protocol-07 §5
  material.
- ~/PROJECT/ietf-mimi-calls, draft-atwood-mimi-calls (328 md lines):
  where a MIMI-backed call's media keys come from. mimi-content and
  mls-extensions material.

draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential targets MLS, not MIMI, so it is
not part of this question.

## Decided: keep them separate, and sequence them

### Why not merge

1. Adoption is per-document. A WG adopts a draft by saying yes to its
   subject, so three mechanisms in one document must be accepted
   together and the least ready sets the ceiling for the rest.
2. They share no subject. Authentication, media keys and fanout
   reliability have in common only that mimid needed them. A document
   whose subject is "what one implementer found missing" has no natural
   reviewer and no shepherd.
3. They land in different documents. provider-auth and catchup are
   protocol material, calls is content material, so a merged draft
   would have to be split again to land.

### The real problem, which merging does not fix

Three drafts from one author compete for the same WG attention and read
as volume rather than signal. 64 open `wg` beads say the same. The
answer is sequencing: push one, let the others sit as written and
available.

### The order

catchUp first. It closes a correctness hole rather than adding a
feature, which is an easier yes, and it carries the implementation
evidence the chairs have wanted since the 2026-01-13 chair message
(6c25801e, 33de78f9, and a two-provider test).

Then provider-auth, which is substantial and already has an epic behind
it (mimid-75nk). calls last, or not as a draft at all -- see below.

## Open, not decided here

Whether draft-atwood-mimi-calls should be a draft at all. If it is
essentially "which component keys the media", a PR or issue against
mimi-content may land more easily and takes a document off the pile
without merging anything. Needs someone to actually read it; the
judgement above is from its size and subject, not its content.

Nothing is sent upstream without Mark's OK (memory:
dont-flood-upstream).
